pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: You can use the local tools and games without an account. An account lets you contribute work and manage your optional research donations. New contributors begin at level 0. Higher permissions require review.

pages.scope: Contributor levels and skills need review. Creating an account does not grant permission to approve scientific claims.
pages.title: Sign in or create an account.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: This is a separate administrative session from your contributor account session. Only accounts explicitly granted administrator authority can enter the Admin Center.
pages.first_step: Sign in with an account that already has administrator permission.
pages.scope: An ordinary contributor session cannot authorize administrative actions.
pages.title: Admin sign in

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: This dashboard is for authorized administrators. Review requests, manage permissions, and inspect the history of administrative actions.
pages.first_step: Sign in to the separate administrator session, then choose the section you need.
pages.scope: Administrative approval and scientific verification are separate decisions. Server permissions control every action.
pages.title: Manage contributions and review decisions.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: PCS keeps the claim, its files, the checks, and the reviewer’s decision separate. This page explains how those parts fit together.
pages.first_step: Follow the workflow diagram, then read the trust boundary for the component you use.
pages.scope: A checked package does not by itself establish that its scientific assumptions or real-world interpretation are correct.
pages.title: How PCS checks a scientific result.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Turn facts on or off, then compare the two results.
pages.first_step: Turn one fact on or off, then check whether the two rules give different answers.
pages.scope: A counterexample is one example where the rules disagree. This checks a small fictional world, not a deployed AI.
pages.title: Find an example where the rules disagree.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Practise putting evidence before a conclusion. Start with building a bridge: each step must have what it needs.
pages.first_step: Tap a step card to add it to your path, then check the completed order.
pages.scope: A working card order practises prerequisites. It is not a mathematical proof.
pages.title: Put the steps in order.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Practise finding a loophole, then fixing it without stopping the job. Your challenge is to protect a fictional bot’s mission.
pages.first_step: Try an action, look for a failure, then switch to fixing the rules.
pages.scope: A repair must prevent failures and still allow the fictional mission. Passing this game does not establish real AI safety.
pages.title: Find the bot’s mistake. Fix its rules.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: PCS checks claims instead of taking their word for it. These games let you practise: try an idea, see why it works or fails, then improve it. No account or coding needed.
pages.first_step: Start with World Builder. Choose the other games when you want a different kind of puzzle.
pages.scope: The games practise finding mistakes and checking ideas. Playing does not automatically share your moves or train a model.
pages.title: Learn to spot a mistake.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Sort statements by what their evidence actually supports. The board gets cooler as you put cards in the right places.
pages.first_step: Choose a card and a category, or drag the card onto the board.
pages.scope: A completed board checks the game categories. It is not scientific approval or a new Lean proof.
pages.title: Sort the cards. Cool the board.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Choose a useful step and watch your bridge grow.
pages.first_step: Start the easy tutorial, then choose step cards that connect the facts to the goal.
pages.scope: The board uses recorded proof steps. A fresh remote Lean check requires a separate request and publication consent.
pages.title: Connect the facts to the goal.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Explore real yacht measurements. Compare predictions with observations that were kept out of the fitting step, then see how the prediction depends on an assumed measurement-error limit.
pages.first_step: Choose a hull, meaning one boat shape. Compare the dots and predictions before changing the error assumption.
pages.scope: The browser calculates exact numerical checks. The Lean proofs are recorded evidence, not a new run here. Physical validity and prediction accuracy on unseen boats remain open.
pages.title: How reliable is a prediction?

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: PCS has several engines. Some tools use trained models to propose an answer. Others calculate an exact result or show an earlier experiment. A model proposal still needs its own check.
pages.first_step: Choose a tool in the execution map to see whether it runs a model, computes a check, or shows a recorded result.
pages.scope: A model suggestion needs checking. Recorded evidence is different from a fresh execution.
pages.title: What actually runs?

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Choose two CSV exports and the column that identifies each person or item. We’ll show you matching IDs and the rows to review.
pages.first_step: Choose two CSV files, select their ID columns, then check for shared IDs.
pages.scope: An ID is the label for a person or item. Only the two chosen columns are checked; a match does not establish data accuracy.
pages.title: Do these files share any IDs?

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Follow how a changed file can affect later calculations and claims. This research task studies when those claims must be reopened.
pages.first_step: Read the small example and contribution packet before choosing a task.
pages.scope: The dependency map only knows the connections that were recorded. It cannot discover an omitted connection automatically.
pages.title: What needs rechecking when a file changes?

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Open a PCS translation plan to see which supporting checks are complete and which questions remain open. The file stays on your device.
pages.first_step: Load the recursive example, or open a compatible translation JSON file.
pages.scope: This page displays a plan. It does not run the production verifier or approve a scientific claim.
pages.title: Follow the evidence behind a claim.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Choose a small task that fits your time and skills. Each task explains what to deliver and how the work will be reviewed.
pages.first_step: Browse the published tasks or the beginner contribution guide.
pages.scope: A completed task can support a larger claim, but only checked evidence can settle that claim.
pages.title: Find a useful way to help PCS.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Tell us what you want to check, which files matter, and what another person would need to repeat the check. Start with a small, non-sensitive example.
pages.first_step: Read the contact options and choose the one that matches your question.
pages.scope: A conversation is not a private-data intake agreement or independent scientific validation.
pages.title: Talk to us about a scientific workflow.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: You can help with research, engineering, testing, writing, or operations. Start with a task that matches your time and skills. An account is required to submit work. Your verified levels are assigned, never self-selected.
pages.first_step: Choose your available time and experience, then review the suggested path.
pages.scope: Open beginner tasks do not require an exam. Reserved or specialist work can require verified skills and manual approval.
pages.title: Choose a way to contribute.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Start with open tasks and build a record of reliable work. More advanced responsibilities require evidence and review.
pages.first_step: Read the level requirements, then use your account to request the next appropriate review.
pages.scope: A contributor level describes permissions and reviewed experience. It does not make someone’s scientific claims automatically true.
pages.title: How contributor levels work.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Change a sample package and inspect which check catches the problem. This is an older, recorded-format demonstration; use it to understand the checks.
pages.first_step: Load the reference package, choose a change, then inspect the resulting rejection.
pages.scope: This browser demonstration uses the frozen v0.5 format. Current authoritative verification uses the separate compiled Lean checker.
pages.title: See how a damaged evidence package is rejected.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Inspect whether a model gives consistent answers when the same logic problem is rewritten. Run the evaluator on your computer, then open its report here.
pages.first_step: Open an evaluator report; optionally load a second report for comparison.
pages.scope: Displayed reports are not trusted until their predictions are recomputed. These public tests are not a blind evaluation.
pages.title: Compare a model’s answers across equivalent questions.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Browse the papers, datasets, standards, and repositories used by the PCS demonstrations. Each entry explains its connection to the project.
pages.first_step: Filter the source list, then open a source or its related demonstration.
pages.scope: A source link is a citation, not evidence that PCS reproduced or verified the entire study.
pages.title: Find the sources behind the examples.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: PCS checks specific rules in data and calculations. It shows what passed, what needs attention, and how someone else can check the same result.
pages.first_step: Run the published-data example, read the result, then save and reopen its recheck file.
pages.scope: The example checks preservation of recorded values. It does not establish that the measurements or scientific conclusions are correct.
pages.title: Check your work.Keep the evidence.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Try a walkthrough or game, then tell us whether you understood it. You can skip a task or stop whenever you want.
pages.first_step: Read the recording explanation, choose whether to consent, then try any practice task.
pages.scope: Records stay on this device until you choose to share a download. Client records do not prove human authorship or reliable timing.
pages.title: Which parts are confusing?

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Compare two robot plans. Pick one, then see what the game checks.
pages.first_step: Read the two bot plans, choose one or neither, then inspect what the simulator finds.
pages.scope: The result concerns the fictional mission and its fixed rules. It does not certify a real bot or AI system.
pages.title: Which plan would you choose?

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Funding can support infrastructure, specialist reviews, and clearly defined contributor tasks. This page explains the proposed funding model and its limits.
pages.first_step: Read the funding categories and contact PCS before making a commitment.
pages.scope: A task is payable only when it is explicitly funded and written terms have been agreed. Funding never purchases a scientific verdict.
pages.title: Help fund useful safety work.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: This page explains who can approve work, how conflicts are handled, and why scientific claims still need evidence.
pages.first_step: Read the responsibilities relevant to your role and the rules for conflicts or paid work.
pages.scope: Governance rules organize people. They cannot substitute for verification or the separate legal terms of an agreement.
pages.title: How decisions and responsibilities work.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Choose the relevant project files, review the checks PCS suggests, and save a draft for someone else to inspect. You confirm what the scientific question means.
pages.first_step: Try the synthetic example, or choose a small non-sensitive part of your project.
pages.scope: A suggested check is a draft. This browser does not execute your code or issue a scientific certificate.
pages.title: Prepare a scientific project for review.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: PCS checks specific rules in data and calculations. It shows what passed, what needs attention, and how someone else can check the same result.
pages.first_step: Try the scientific example first. Then use the file tools, model walkthrough, or research pages.
pages.scope: Each tool checks a particular question. Its result must be read with its assumptions and limits.
pages.title: Check your work.Keep the evidence.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Define the project, the specific questions, and the assumptions before looking at the result. Save that agreed description for the later review.
pages.first_step: Fill in the pilot’s question and scope, then validate and export the description.
pages.scope: Locking a description helps detect later changes. It does not check the underlying science or sign an approval.
pages.title: Write down what you want checked.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Change the allowed facts and check whether your plan reaches its goal.
pages.first_step: Choose a mission, change the permitted facts, then check whether your plan reaches the goal.
pages.scope: The cheapest plan is calculated only for the displayed Boolean variables, costs, and constraints.
pages.title: Find a lower-cost plan.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Choose a supported mathematical question, try proof steps, and inspect the result. For a guided start, open the proof workbench.
pages.first_step: Use the proof workbench for a guided start, or connect the local backend for interactive proof play.
pages.scope: Lean checks an exact mathematical statement. Your intended English meaning still needs review. Public jobs require explicit publication consent.
pages.title: Explore how PCS searches for a proof.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Change the facts about a fictional tool call and compare the original rule with its rewrite. Find a case where the rules give different answers.
pages.first_step: Turn a fact on or off, then inspect both rule outcomes.
pages.scope: The browser checks finite logic. Separate server replay is explicit; this does not test the behaviour of a real AI.
pages.title: Can a rewrite change a safety rule?

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Change the controls until the proposed sentence matches the target.
pages.first_step: Choose a mission and change a word or relationship until the proposed sentence matches its target.
pages.scope: This game checks its controlled sentence structure. It does not establish arbitrary English meaning or compile Lean.
pages.title: Make the words mean the same thing.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Connect the facts to the goal using the rules in your toolbox.
pages.first_step: Start the easy tutorial, then choose a checked rule to help connect the facts to the goal.
pages.scope: Recorded proof steps and fresh kernel checks are separate. A reused rule still has to fit the current exact goal.
pages.title: Use a checked rule again.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Change the dose and model parameters, calculate the predicted concentrations, and save the files needed for a separate PCS check.
pages.first_step: Choose model parameters, generate predictions, then inspect or download them.
pages.scope: This is a restricted mathematical model. It is not medical advice or evidence that a dose is safe or effective.
pages.title: Explore a simple drug-concentration model.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Models can suggest plausible changes that are wrong. PCS keeps the suggestion separate from the check. Try a small example of that process.
pages.first_step: Choose an example, ask the actual trained ranker for a repair, then inspect the separate checks.
pages.scope: Passing means agreement in the registered small worlds. It does not prove real AI safety or equivalence in all possible worlds.
pages.title: A model suggests.A checker tests.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Prepare a small scientific project, collect its evidence, and let an independent reviewer repeat the supported checks. This page gives the command-line setup.
pages.first_step: Start with the guided project mapper, then follow the producer and reviewer commands.
pages.scope: These instructions require a local technical setup. Use Start here for a no-installation introduction.
pages.title: Run PCS on your own computer.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Choose an example or write an explicit interpretation. Follow the supporting questions and compare search strategies, including trained models.
pages.first_step: Load an example, then select a claim or supporting question in the graph.
pages.scope: The workspace checks explicit Boolean interpretations. It does not automatically understand a paper or run the production authority.
pages.title: Map a claim and its supporting evidence.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Learn about public access, research collaboration, and the proposed commercial support model. Contact PCS to discuss a concrete workflow. We discuss support and service requirements with large commercial organizations.
pages.first_step: Choose the use case closest to your organization and read what would need agreement.
pages.scope: These are access and sustainability plans, not a signed service contract or a promise of enterprise readiness.
pages.title: Using PCS as an organization.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: A PCS package keeps a claim and its evidence together in one file. Open it to see the contents and check their recorded file identities.
pages.first_step: Load the sample package, or choose a compatible .pcs.zip file.
pages.scope: Browser inspection is not authoritative verification. The recipient must run the appropriate independent verifier before relying on a package.
pages.title: Inspect an evidence package.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Start with the Palmer Penguins field measurements, inspect the evidence behind the calculation, and see what was checked and what remains uncertain.
pages.first_step: Choose a demonstration and follow its source, calculation, evidence, and limits.
pages.scope: The page shows recorded verification receipts. A successful computational check does not validate an entire study or its biological interpretation.
pages.title: Explore scientific examples with published data.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Local tools keep their working data on your device. Accounts, public proof requests, and optional research donations have different data rules, explained below.
pages.first_step: Read the section for the feature you use before signing in, publishing a proof request, or donating research data.
pages.scope: Publication, research consent, account erasure, exported copies, and infrastructure logs have separate effects. Local calculations do not imply zero website logging.
pages.title: What PCS stores and shares.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Inspect files locally and review the checks PCS proposes. This advanced tool gives direct control over the draft and its technical details. Nothing is uploaded, and your code is not executed.
pages.first_step: Choose a project folder or load the synthetic example, then review the suggested files and checks.
pages.scope: Your code is not executed or uploaded. The output is a draft, not a verified scientific result.
pages.title: Choose which project files to check.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Follow the connections from a task to the question it supports. See which work and evidence are still needed.
pages.first_step: Choose a published project, then inspect its tasks and supporting evidence.
pages.scope: A finished task is not itself a proof. Only the appropriate verified evidence can settle the scientific question.
pages.title: See how a task helps a larger project.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: The stronger symbolic strategy solved more of these questions. The learned policy did not add a uniquely solved question. That is why the workbench offers the fast checked portfolio first.
pages.first_step: Compare the two methods, then inspect the retained results and their limits.
pages.scope: The learned policy showed no unique solved question in this study. The small authored set is not a general measure of mathematical intelligence.
pages.title: What worked in our proof-search test?

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: This optional pilot asks whether people can use the workbench and understand what a result means. Software cannot establish that a participant is human or inexperienced. We have no human pilot results yet.
pages.first_step: Read the consent and task instructions before starting any optional recording.
pages.scope: Human origin, prior experience and timing need independent observation. No human usability result is established by the software.
pages.title: Help us test the proof workflow.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: See exactly what you are asking, let a proof strategy try it, and keep evidence someone else can check.
pages.first_step: Choose a supported question, review its exact meaning, then try a recorded example or explicitly publish a real proof job.
pages.scope: A recorded example is not a fresh run. A fresh Lean result checks the displayed statement and assumptions, not its real-world meaning.
pages.title: Check a mathematical claim.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Pick a card, see whether it is ready, and build an investigation.
pages.first_step: Choose an investigation card whose required starting facts are ready.
pages.scope: This is a planning exercise around recorded mathematical material. Completing the graph does not itself prove a theorem.
pages.title: Choose what to check next.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Choose a logic example, change its assumptions, and look for a case where the conclusion fails. You decide what each variable means.
pages.first_step: Start with an example, then change one assumption or fact and rerun the check.
pages.scope: The calculation concerns explicit Boolean formulas. It does not establish the truth of an assumption in the real world.
pages.title: Which assumptions does your conclusion need?

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Choose a case and inspect how a trained model ranks possible edits.
pages.first_step: Choose a case and ask the trained model to rank edits. Inspect the finite check for each attempted repair.
pages.scope: A model score suggests what to try. Only the separate finite evaluator establishes agreement within the displayed bound.
pages.title: Watch a model suggest repairs.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Change an input, run a real browser calculation, and see why a check passes or fails. Follow the links to the separate evidence-review workflow. No account required.
pages.first_step: Choose an example, change one input, then run its check.
pages.scope: These are synthetic browser examples. They do not run Lean or establish that a deployed AI or scientific model is valid.
pages.title: Try a small scientific or policy check.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Explore the integrated proofs and experiments, the exact inputs they concern, and the questions that remain open.
pages.first_step: Choose a research area, then read its result, assumptions, evidence and reproduction instructions.
pages.scope: An unsigned website summary is not an independent review. Recorded proofs must be replayed with their exact trusted sources.
pages.title: Research results and their limits.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: People and AI models can propose results. PCS studies how separate checks can establish precisely what those results support.
pages.first_step: Start with a bounded claim below, then follow the related evidence or technical architecture.
pages.scope: Research goals are not all released capabilities. Mathematical truth, implementation correspondence and empirical validity are separate.
pages.title: What PCS research is trying to establish.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Try to reproduce a result, expose a missed error, or identify an assumption that needs more evidence. Start with a small, agreed scope.
pages.first_step: Choose a type of evaluation and agree on non-sensitive inputs and the expected checks.
pages.scope: A pilot is an evaluation, not an endorsement. Private data and research agreements require separate arrangements.
pages.title: Help test a PCS scientific workflow.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Read four separate answers: were the files intact, did the computation pass, was the formal evidence valid, and did the reviewer accept it?
pages.first_step: Choose a result example, then inspect each answer and its explanation.
pages.scope: A valid package can contain a failed claim. A supported calculation can still be rejected by a reviewer.
pages.title: How to read a PCS result.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Compare two CSV files. See added, removed and edited records, then check the changes against your rules. Your files stay on this device.
pages.first_step: Choose the previous and new CSV exports, select their ID columns, then choose which values and changes matter.
pages.scope: The result checks selected records and rules. It does not establish whether a changed value is scientifically correct.
pages.title: What changed since the last export?

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Read a submitted explanation and check whether it accurately describes its evidence. Only eligible, independent reviewers can submit a decision.
pages.first_step: Sign in with an eligible contributor account, then load the next review items.
pages.scope: A structured game score does not validate prose. Two eligible, non-conflicting reviews are required before text enters the approved export.
pages.title: Review a contributed explanation.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Roles cover recurring responsibilities such as operations, communications, and community work. Apply for a role that matches your experience and availability.
pages.first_step: Read an opening and its scope, then submit the requested application.
pages.scope: A role does not reserve a research task or automatically grant scientific or administrative authority.
pages.title: Find an ongoing role.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Compare penguin species and inspect individual observations. Then follow the source data, calculation, and recorded verification evidence.
pages.first_step: Select a dot or a species to explore the data, then read the recorded check and its limits.
pages.scope: The plot recalculates in the browser. The signed package results are recorded; no new Lean run or biological validation occurs here.
pages.title: Explore real penguin measurements.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Choose a translation example and see what its recorded test expected. The cases come from an archived Aristotle proof-development output. This page is not executing Lean.
pages.first_step: Choose a translation change and compare the intended meaning with the recorded expectation.
pages.scope: These are archived fixture expectations. This page does not execute Lean or independently establish a fresh verification verdict.
pages.title: Inspect examples of changed meaning.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Change the facts and test whether a translation changes a rule.

pages.scope: Agreement is limited to the displayed finite domain. Public evaluation families are inspectable, not a blind test.
pages.title: Spot a change in meaning.

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Choose a case, run the search, and inspect what it found.

pages.title: Watch a repair search work.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Follow the arrows to see what a task needs before it can begin. Some tasks need every input; others need one of several alternatives.

pages.scope: The map shows declared dependencies and accepted outputs. It cannot establish connections that were never recorded.
pages.title: See which tasks need other work first.

pages.purpose: Browse work that PCS has explicitly marked as needed. Only work the project owner has approved for publication appears here. Choose a task with a clear deliverable, review rule, and finish line.

pages.scope: Only published needed work appears. Paid work requires explicit funding and written terms; applying does not guarantee acceptance.
pages.title: Find a task you can help with.

pages.scope: The data is synthetic. The animation is a browser visualization; recorded package checks do not establish physical accuracy.
pages.title: Follow material moving between five compartments.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: Compare mathematical proofs, executed software checks, and assumptions that still require trust. Each card explains one part of PCS.
pages.first_step: Filter the cards, then read both the supported claim and its remaining limits.
pages.scope: A green check is meaningful only for its stated question. These categories must not be treated as one blanket approval.
pages.title: See what each kind of check establishes.

pages.changes: rewrote title/intro and added contextual help
pages.purpose: See which capabilities are released, which mathematical results are proved, which checks were executed, and what remains uncertain.
pages.first_step: Start with the status summary, then follow the evidence for the feature you use.
pages.scope: A proof about a mathematical statement does not prove its inputs describe reality or that a whole scientific study is valid.
pages.title: What can you rely on in PCS?

pages.changes: retained clear title/intro; added page-specific instructions and scope
pages.purpose: Try the file tools with practice data. This helps identify unclear steps. You can use PCS without taking part.

pages.scope: Answers and times are unverified client records. Actual newcomer findings require separate observation and consent.
pages.title: Can you finish these tasks without help?

pages.purpose: Inspect the examples used to test PCS, including cases that should pass and cases that should fail.
pages.first_step: Filter the list, then open a case and inspect its expected and recorded outcome.
pages.scope: This page displays committed results. It does not rerun the checks or establish performance on every scientific workflow.
pages.title: Browse the published validation cases.

pages.purpose: Three cases were expected to pass and two were deliberately expected to fail. The recorded checks matched all five expectations.
